results.notes: Reproduction source: Exp1_model.xlsx, Sheet1, Excel rows 2-205; PT=1 is LLM partner (n=104), PT=0 is human partner (n=100). TC=0 is the simple tire task and TC=1 is the complex VR task. The treatment task cells contain 52 people each and control cells contain 50 each. All 204 analysis-file participants have outcome and both mediators; no participant exclusions or imputations were made. Arm counts are printed in supplement PDF p. 10, Table S5; study N=204 is also in main-paper Fig. 2. The ten deposited workbooks were verified against their manifest SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes. The computed object uses Exp1_creativity_rating.xlsx: average the two expert ratings on each idea, then average all of a participant's ideas with equal idea weights. There are 1093 ideas and 204 participants, all with two complete ratings per idea. The idea-only workbook matches the rating workbook's idea, user, timestamp and room columns exactly. IDs such as (C)NAI31 are normalized to NAI31C; the full-width opening parenthesis in survey IDs is normalized as well. These IDs denote distinct between-person task cells, not repeat rounds. Computed means and sample SDs weight people equally; SD uses n-1. Difference is treatment minus control on the original 1-5 creativity scale. Difference SE is from OLS of the participant outcome on an intercept and the arm indicator with HC2, independently checked against sqrt(s_t^2/n_t + s_c^2/n_c). Individual randomization requires no clusters. There is no paired or first-round estimate. Reconstructed mean fixation ratings agree with every analysis-file CF value. Partner-message rows without participant ratings are omitted from this covariate audit. The survey has 3 trailing demographic-summary rows without IDs; these are not people. The complete author-provided IS covariate is used for publication-model reproduction. Every C value in Exp1_model.xlsx agrees with the participant mean independently reconstructed from the ratings (absolute discrepancy below 1e-12). Survey IDs contain HH39C twice and omit HH40C; one HH39C row agrees with its model IS=2.4 and the other has IS=2.0. The model carries IS=2.0 for HH40C, but that survey-ID repair cannot be confirmed and is not performed here. No survey rows are used to exclude people from the complete model or the ratings. Publication checks use main PDF p. 5: pooled expert-creativity means, participant SDs, equal-variance t with df=202 and its two-sided p. The printed t is human minus LLM, opposite the positive treatment-minus-control sign in computed. The paper does not identify the d standardizer or the confidence-interval estimand; neither is guessed or used in this reanalysis.

Reproduction source: Exp2_model.xlsx, Sheet1, Excel rows 2-205; NC=1 is constrained-responsive LLM (n=104), NC=0 is batch-responsive LLM (n=100). TC=0 is the simple tire task and TC=1 is the complex VR task. The treatment task cells contain 52 people each and control cells contain 50 each. All 204 analysis-file participants have outcome and both mediators; no participant exclusions or imputations were made. Arm counts are printed in supplement PDF p. 11, Table S6; study N=204 is also in main-paper Fig. 4. The ten deposited workbooks were verified against their manifest SHA-256 hashes and byte sizes. The computed object uses Exp2_creativity_rating.xlsx: average the two expert ratings on each idea, then average all of a participant's ideas with equal idea weights. There are 1204 ideas and 204 participants, all with two complete ratings per idea. The idea-only workbook matches the rating workbook's idea, user, timestamp and room columns exactly. IDs such as (C)NAI31 are normalized to NAI31C; the full-width opening parenthesis in survey IDs is normalized as well. These IDs denote distinct between-person task cells, not repeat rounds. Computed means and sample SDs weight people equally; SD uses n-1. Difference is treatment minus control on the original 1-5 creativity scale. Difference SE is from OLS of the participant outcome on an intercept and the arm indicator with HC2, independently checked against sqrt(s_t^2/n_t + s_c^2/n_c). Individual randomization requires no clusters. There is no paired or first-round estimate. Reconstructed mean fixation ratings agree with every analysis-file CF value. Partner-message rows without participant ratings are omitted from this covariate audit. The survey has 3 trailing demographic-summary rows without IDs; these are not people. The complete author-provided IS covariate is used for publication-model reproduction. Raw-rating discrepancy: {"NAI31C": {"C": 2.07142857142857, "C_from_ratings": 2.0357142857142856, "n_ideas": 14}}. Specifically, Exp2_model.xlsx F82 gives NAI31C C=2.07142857142857. Its 14 ideas in creativity-rating Excel rows 449-462 have thirteen (2,2) rating pairs and one (3,2), so the required two-rater/within-person average is 2.0357142857142856. The other 203 C values agree. All publication checks in reproduced use the supplied model C; the computed object uses the actual rating averages, without changing any posted rating or copying the discrepant aggregate. Using the reconstructed ratings instead, the original factorial F is 0.824335134876534 (p=0.365008407652797), and the standardized direct coefficient is 0.0300468868225585; these would round to 0.824, 0.365 and 0.030 rather than the printed 0.811, 0.369 and 0.029. Thus publication reproduction succeeds on the authors' deposited analysis table, but exact reconstruction of its outcome from the ratings fails for one person. All 204 survey IS item means match model IS. Arm coding is additionally confirmed by the response-quantity manipulation means: NC=0 gives 4.040 and NC=1 gives 3.058, as printed on main PDF p. 6. Publication checks use main PDF p. 6 factorial response-type F, p, df and partial eta-squared, plus main PDF p. 7 task-cell means to confirm the arm and complexity mapping. The F is the equally weighted main effect from the full treatment-by-complexity model, not the simple pooled t-test squared. Its partial eta-squared is F/(F+200). The new HC2 difference is the pooled contrast requested in the brief, not the factorial model's conventional SE.

Every C value in Exp1_model.xlsx agrees with the participant mean independently reconstructed from the ratings (absolute discrepancy below 1e-12). Survey IDs contain HH39C twice and omit HH40C; one HH39C row agrees with its model IS=2.4 and the other has IS=2.0. The model carries IS=2.0 for HH40C, but that survey-ID repair cannot be confirmed and is not performed here. No survey rows are used to exclude people from the complete model or the ratings. Adjusted reproduction: supplement PDF p. 12, Table S7, Model 4. OLS z(C) on intercept, the unstandardized 0/1 assigned-arm indicator, z(CF), and z(IS) reproduces the treatment coefficient, both mediator coefficients, model R-squared and model F at their printed precision. Each continuous variable is centered and divided by its sample SD across the 204 complete cases. This scaling is an inference supported by the numerical reproduction; the supplement itself does not specify it. Task complexity and its interaction are absent from this outcome equation. The conventional OLS treatment SE is 0.229646201146073, which numerically rounds to the printed 0.230; however, the table note calls the SE bootstrapped with 10,000 replications. The original bootstrap draws/seed are not provided, so bootstrap precision is not claimed as reproduced and is not in the reproduced list. The count checks are explicitly experiment-level printed counts; this table prints no model-specific n. The deposited complete-case model has exactly those 204 people. Per the brief's requested OLS-on-arm computation, computed contains raw unadjusted means and their HC2 difference, not the mediator-adjusted coefficient. Its computed fields duplicate the corresponding pooled record; do not count them as an independent effect.
